items_missed: Never asked for or used the customer's name (Reginald Johnson) at any point in the call, despite the customer introducing himself
No 'How are you today?' opener, and no agenda statement or explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before diving into move details
Didn't ask about additional rooms (garage, storage, balcony), storage needs, or moving stressors ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
No 'pricing is super simple' opener and no explicit hourly rate stated (per mover, per hour) — only a lump-sum total ($840 for 4 hours) was given

No mention of what's included (gas, truck, insurance, wrap pads, tools), disassembly/reassembly, No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, or the no-hidden-fees pitch anywhere in the pricing discussion
Clock mechanics never explained — no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute proration, no mention of when the clock starts
Never stated the number of movers or trucks assigned to the job
No equivalents/analogy or traffic variable mentioned when walking through the estimate range
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech omitted — no consolidation tips, no 'take a carload' tip, no framing that prep = shorter move = lower bill
No deposit and hours/how-to-reach-us were not mentioned in the close
No rapport-building, humor, or insurance (No Worries / 60 cent per lb) explanation offered anywhere on the call
top_strength: Garrison pulled up the existing booking quickly and confirmed every concrete detail accurately (unit number, 725 sq ft one-bedroom, first floor, 150-foot walk, box count, no special items), then gave the customer a specific, transparent estimate adjustment ($840 for 4 hours) and clearly answered his follow-up question about travel-time billing without hesitation.
coaching_note: This call never touched a single differentiator or the Save Your Ass prep speech — Garrison should use the estimate-confirmation moment to mention at least No Worries Damage Coverage and the no-deposit policy, and give the 'take a carload / consolidate loose items' tip, since this was the customer's only live phone touchpoint before move day.
phone_presence_notes: Tone is friendly and polite with frequent affirmations ('perfect, perfect', 'gotcha, gotcha', 'no worries'), but the language is repetitive and transactional and Garrison never personalizes the call by using the customer's name.
